fix_commit_message:
avcodec/jpeg2000dec: clear array length when freeing it

Fixes NULL pointer dereferences.
Fixes ticket #11393.

Reviewed-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 7f9c7f9849a2 on top of intro 80344959f064 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The `av_freep(&cblk->lengthinc)` call at line 1080 frees the `lengthinc` array and sets the pointer to NULL, but does not reset `cblk->nb_lengthinc` to 0. When `jpeg2000_decode_packet` is called again for the same code block (e.g., across multiple tile parts in a JPEG2000 stream), the stale `nb_lengthinc` value causes the for loop at line 1051 to execute, attempting to dereference the now-NULL `cblk->lengthinc` pointer at line 1052 (`cblk->lengthinc[cwsno]`). The guard at line 1049 (`!cblk->nb_terminationsinc && !cblk->lengthinc`) does not prevent this because `nb_terminationsinc` may be non-zero in a subsequent call, causing the `continue` to be skipped. This results in a SEGV (NULL pointer dereference) that can be triggered by a crafted JPEG2000 file, causing denial of service. Assigned CVE-2025-22921. Root cause: When commit 80344959 added `av_freep(&cblk->lengthinc)` to free the lengthinc array earlier for memory optimization, it neglected to also reset `cblk->nb_lengthinc` to 0. The `av_freep` macro sets the pointer to NULL, but the loop counter remains non-zero, creating an inconsistent state. On a subsequent call to the function for the same code block, the guard condition `!cblk->nb_terminationsinc && !cblk->lengthinc` can be bypassed (when `nb_terminationsinc` is non-zero), and the stale `nb_lengthinc` causes the code to dereference the NULL `lengthinc` pointer.
